title: Huge new blow for famous but troubled UK seaside town - '£6m black hole'
excerpt: The revised proposal would reduce the venue's maximum capacity to 5,000 people.
content:
The revised proposal would reduce the venue's maximum capacity to 5,000 people.

12:59, Fri, Nov 6, 2026 Updated: 13:02, Fri, Nov 6, 2026

The Tropicana in Weston-super-mare (Image: Google Maps)

A major regeneration project in a troubled seaside town has been thrown into doubt after a £6.6million funding shortfall forced the local council to reconsider its plans. North Somerset Council is proposing to halve the size of a planned entertainment arena at the Tropicana in Weston-super-Mare, after failing to secure the money needed to deliver the original scheme.

The former seafront lido was due to be transformed into a 10,000-capacity venue under a 25-year agreement with entertainment giant Live Nation. However, the original plans would require the council to find an additional £6.6million, prompting it to consider a smaller and potentially more affordable alternative.

The revised proposal would see the maximum capacity reduced to 5,000 people, with the council still intending to turn the building into a major events space capable of hosting community activities. Councillors are due to decide on November 10 how much the local authority should contribute towards the proposed 25-year lease arrangement with Live Nation.

The revised scheme could include a refurbished promenade building, indoor event space, repairs to the sea wall, essential infrastructure improvements, modern facilities and better accessibility. But the scaled-back plans also raise questions about whether Live Nation will remain committed to the project.

The entertainment company agreed to operate the Tropicana for 25 years, with the deal announced to considerable fanfare in May. At the time, council leader Mike Bell described the agreement as a "game-changer" for the town, reported the BBC.

However, the funding gap was already apparent when the deal was announced, with Mr Bell acknowledging a £6million hole in the budget.

He said at the time: "My expectation is that we're not looking for council tax payers to put money in."

The latest developments suggest the money has not materialised, with negotiations with Live Nation apparently failing to provide the funding or certainty needed to proceed with the original scheme.

The council is now looking at a smaller venue as a way of making the project more financially deliverable.

Councillor Bell said the revised approach was based on "practicality and deliverability", while recognising the potential impact of the venue on the surrounding area.

He added: "Ultimately, this is about finding the right balance for Weston, being ambitious for the future of the Tropicana while making sure we deliver something that works for residents, visitors and businesses over the long-term."

The proposals follow concerns from local residents about the impact of a large events venue on the town.

Some have raised questions about transport links, parking pressures and the potential effect on the beach lawns and wider seafront.

The council said its recommended approach was intended to balance its ambitions for the Tropicana with concerns raised by the community.

It added that significant details of the revised offer would still need further work before an arrangement with Live Nation could be finalised.

The Tropicana has been derelict for years and has been at the centre of efforts to regenerate Weston-super-Mare's seafront.

The original 10,000-capacity arena was seen as a major opportunity to attract large-scale concerts and events to the Somerset resort.

But the proposed reduction in capacity represents a significant scaling-back of those ambitions, with the future of the long-awaited redevelopment now dependent on the council's decision and further negotiations with Live Nation.
